assertion.text:
Erdős Problem #912: declared status 'open'. Formalized: yes. If\[n! = \prod_i p_i^{k_i}\]is the factorisation into distinct primes then let $h(n)$ count the number of distinct exponents $k_i$.

Prove that there exists some $c>0$ such that\[h(n) \sim c \left(\frac{n}{\log n}\right)^{1/2}\]as $n\to \infty$. Prize: no. OEIS: A071626. Tags: factorials, number theory.
